title: Kanva's three kinds of father
hookLine: a baby left by a river, birds standing guard, and the sage who says what makes a father
carry: life, safety and food each make a father
last: A MARRIAGE IS VOWED WITH THE GODS AS WITNESS.

cards: A newborn lies alone on a riverbank in the forest. No mother nearby. No village.

And around her, keeping off whatever might come out of the trees, are birds. That's how the Mahabharata's first book begins the life of Shakuntala, a stranger start than the love story people remember. A king will come.
Today we stay before he arrives, with a girl, the birds, and the old hermit who heard her cry.

teach.b: In the epic, Shakuntala tells her own beginning to a visitor, the way she heard it from the sage Kanva, who raised her.

It starts with another sage, Vishvamitra, whose austerities are so fierce that Indra, king of the gods, grows afraid of his power. Indra sends the apsara Menaka, a celestial dancer, to break his concentration. She does.
A daughter is born. Menaka leaves the baby beside a river in the forest and goes back to heaven. So the girl's parents are a great sage and a heavenly woman, and neither stays.
Then the birds gather around the baby and protect her in that lonely place. Kanva, out for his bath, finds her, brings her home to his hermitage and raises her as his daughter.

teach.h: LEFT BY THE RIVER, GUARDED BY BIRDS
teach.b: He names her for the birds: the epic's word for bird is shakunta, so she is Shakuntala, the one the birds protected.

teach.h: KANVA NAMES HER FOR THE BIRDS
teach.b: Then Kanva says the line this day is built on.

teach.h: LIFE, SAFETY AND FOOD EACH MAKE A FATHER.
teach.b: The dharma texts, he says, count three as a father: the one who gives the body, the one who saves a life, and the one who gives food. By that measure, he is fully her father.
That's the teaching, in the tradition's own words: in dharma, a parent is made by giving life, by keeping safe and by feeding, not by birth alone. And it lands right in modern families.

An uncle who raised a nephew, a stepdad who packed the lunches, a grandmother who fed a child through the hard years: Kanva's words already count them. Her name doesn't remember her well-known parents.
It remembers the birds who stood guard, and the old man who chose her.

how: Hindus know Shakuntala's story from the Mahabharata's first book, the Adi Parva, and from the poet Kalidasa's later play about her; her birth is told in both.

o: a girl named for the river where her mother bathed
a princess named for her mother, a well-known dancer
a girl named for the birds that guarded her as a baby

games.q: where Shakuntala came from — tap the pairs.
p: the sage whose austerities alarmed Indra
the apsara who left the baby by the river
guarded the baby in the forest
found her and raised her as his daughter

s: Shakuntala was raised by her birth mother in the forest
Menaka left her by the river and went back to heaven; the sage Kanva raised her.
in the epic, her name comes from the birds that protected her
Kanva named her from shakunta, bird.
Kanva says only the one who gives life counts as a father
he names three: the one who gives life, the one who saves it, and the one who gives food.

games.q: someone tells Shakuntala that Kanva isn't her real father, since he didn't give her life. what would Kanva answer?
o: they're right; only the father by birth counts.
three are counted as father: who gives the body, who saves a life, who gives food.
a father is whoever names the child.
games.why: Kanva says the dharma texts count three as father. he saved her and fed her, so by that measure he is fully her father.

practice: Bring to mind someone you keep safe or feed right now: a child, a parent, a neighbor, a friend, an animal.
On the in-breath let them come into view; on the out-breath, picture yourself standing near them, the way the birds stood around the baby. If you pray, you can hold them in prayer.

wordCard.voice: Shakuntala. The girl left by the river, guarded by birds, and named for them by the sage who made himself her father.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the epic explains it from shakunta, bird: the one the birds protected.

carryVoice: Your line: life, safety and food each make a father. Kanva gave her two of the three, and that was enough. That's today, done.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (Shakuntala tells her birth as Kanva told it: Vishvamitra's austerities; Indra sends Menaka; the baby left by the Malini river; the birds; Kanva finds and names her; Kanva's words on who is a father)
